name: Tier list ranking
structure: Place items into S/A/B/C/D tiers one at a time with a quick justification.
hook: "[Topic] tier list" with the empty grid on screen (green screen or template).
middle: Drag each item into a tier with one sentence of reasoning. The controversial placements drive comments.
ending: Full tier grid shown; "what would you move?"
adapt: The final grid works as a standalone image on X/LinkedIn ("AI tools tier list 2026"). @danvmartell: 8.9M on TikTok.

name: "Things I wish I knew" list
structure: The creator lists 3 lessons they learned the hard way in a field.
hook: "3 things I wish I knew before [starting X]".
middle: Numbered points (First / Second / Finally), each with a short reason.
ending: Encouraging closer ("be consistent, trust me").
adapt: The same list converts directly into a carousel or a LinkedIn text post. It works as a TikTok photo carousel too (@elle_kvl 11.8M).

name: Price ladder / cheap vs expensive test
structure: Test the same item at rising price points ($1 → $1,000) side by side and crown a winner.
hook: Show both items on screen in frame 1 with price labels: "$1 knife vs $1,000 knife".
middle: Same test on each (cut, taste, drop). Cut hard between tiers; price tag stays on screen.
ending: Verdict, ideally a twist (cheap one wins, or it's a tie). Ask "what should we test next?"
adapt: Text-free visual test, so it travels as-is. For LinkedIn/X, cut it into a two-image comparison post ("$9/mo tool vs $299/mo tool") and put the verdict in the text.

name: POV skit
structure: First-person role-play of a relatable situation, 'POV: you…'.
hook: "POV: …" text overlay over the first line of dialogue.
middle: One scene, 1–3 characters (often the same creator), escalating.
ending: Punchline or relatable twist.
adapt: Works on every video app. LinkedIn only takes office or industry POVs ('POV: the client asks for one more revision').

name: Street interview (one question to strangers)
structure: Stop strangers with one repeatable question and cut the best answers together.
hook: The question as text plus the first surprising answer within 2s.
middle: Fast montage of answers, or one deep exchange.
ending: Wildest answer last, or a wholesome payoff.
adapt: Subtitles have to be burned in. Travels unchanged across the video apps; LinkedIn likes the 'what do you do and how much do you make' version.
good_for: finance ('what do you do for a living')

name: Rating / blind ranking / taste test
structure: Try items one by one, score each out of 10 or rank blind before seeing the next.
hook: "Rating every X" or "Blind ranking X" plus the lineup on screen.
middle: One item per beat with an honest reaction; a running scoreboard on screen.
ending: Final ranking card, and a hot take that invites disagreement.
adapt: Long TikToks (3–9 min) need a sub-60s cut for Shorts/Reels. Post the final ranking card as a standalone image on X/LinkedIn.

name: Unboxing / first impressions
structure: Open a package on camera with the reveal as the payoff.
hook: The box and the promise ("world's biggest mystery bag").
middle: Slow reveal of each item, ASMR sound.
ending: The best item and a reaction.
adapt: Travels as-is.

name: Types of people
structure: Act out 4–8 archetypes of people in one setting.
hook: "Types of people at the gym / on planes" plus the first type in 1s.
middle: One labeled archetype per beat (text label on each).
ending: The most relatable or absurd type last; "which one are you?"
adapt: Also works as a 'which one are you' carousel (Canva's archetype carousel: 10.2K likes, 233 comments).

name: Overhead quick recipe
structure: Top-down, fast-cut recipe from raw ingredients to the final bite.
hook: The final dish or the 'money shot' first, plus the name ("one pan breakfast sandwich").
middle: Each step 1–3s, ingredients as text overlay.
ending: Cut, cheese pull, or first bite.
adapt: Put the full recipe in the caption on IG/TikTok and in a pinned comment on Shorts.

name: X explained in 60 seconds
structure: Compress a complex topic into one minute with a visual aid.
hook: "[Topic] explained in 60 seconds" or the core question.
middle: 3–5 beats building understanding: whiteboard, b-roll, or a clip from an expert.
ending: A one-line takeaway.
adapt: Keep it under 60s so it stays eligible everywhere. The LinkedIn version adds a text summary.

name: Wrong answers only (comment-bait game)
structure: Ask a question where everyone deliberately answers wrong, for laughs and comments.
hook: "Wrong answers only" plus the question.
middle: Rapid wrong answers from a group.
ending: The most absurd answer last.
adapt: The brand version is a single image plus 'wrong answers only' on X/IG; comments do the work.

name: Before/after transformation (then vs now, 1 day vs 1 year)
structure: Show the start state, then the end state after time or effort.
hook: The 'before' with a date or label, and the promise of the 'after'.
middle: Transition (snap, clap, or wipe) or a fast timelapse of progress.
ending: The 'after' held long enough to replay.
adapt: As a carousel it's 2 slides (before/after photos). On LinkedIn/X it's a 'then vs now' chart or dashboard screenshot.

name: Guess the price (game with a stake)
structure: Host asks someone to guess a price; if they're close they win it.
hook: "Guess the price and it's yours" plus the item on camera.
middle: The guess, then the reveal. Tension from the stake.
ending: Win or lose reaction, then a hand-off to the next item or person.
adapt: Long TikTok versions (2–3 min) should be cut under 60s for Shorts, with an earlier reveal.

name: Rich vs poor / class-contrast skit
structure: The same situation acted out twice, 'rich' vs 'poor' (or broke vs wealthy habits).
hook: Split label "RICH vs POOR" plus the situation.
middle: Alternate cuts between the two versions and escalate the contrast.
ending: Punchline or reversal, e.g. the 'poor' one is smarter.
adapt: The finance/habits version ("rich habits vs poor habits") also works as a LinkedIn/IG carousel.

name: Satisfying process / how it's made
structure: Uninterrupted footage of a process from raw input to finished result, with no talking.
hook: Frame 1 is already mid-action (press coming down, blade touching).
middle: Continuous steps, ASMR sound, few or no cuts.
ending: The finished object, or a loop back to the start so it replays.
adapt: No language, so it goes everywhere untouched. On LinkedIn it works as a factory or 'how our product is made' clip with a 1-line caption.

name: Life hack / "you've been doing it wrong"
structure: Show the common way, call it wrong, then show a better trick.
hook: "You've been doing X wrong your whole life" plus the wrong way on screen.
middle: The trick, shown step by step in close-up.
ending: Result shot, often with a 'save this' prompt.
adapt: Works on every video platform. On X/LinkedIn post it as a screen-recording GIF with 'most people do X, do Y instead'.

name: Unpopular opinion / hot take
structure: State a contrarian opinion bluntly and let the comments argue.
hook: "Unpopular opinion:" plus the take in 1 line.
middle: Short defense (or none; text-only versions work).
ending: "Agree or disagree?"
adapt: One of the strongest LinkedIn/X text formats. The same line works as a text post.

name: Expectation vs reality / Instagram vs reality
structure: The polished version first, then the messy truth.
hook: "Expectation" or "Instagram" label over the glossy shot.
middle: Hard cut to "Reality". Repeat 2–5 pairs.
ending: Funniest or most honest pair last.
adapt: As a carousel it becomes a 2-slide before/after. LinkedIn: 'what the job posting said vs the actual job'.

name: Would you rather / this or that
structure: Two options per screen; the viewer picks before the timer or reveal.
hook: The first choice pair on screen within 1s.
middle: 10–20 rapid pairs with a timer and vote percentages.
ending: The hardest pair last; "comment your score".
adapt: Works as an IG carousel poll (one pair per slide) and as X polls.

name: Day in the life (incl. what I eat in a day)
structure: Timestamped montage of one day in a specific role or life.
hook: "Day in the life of a [specific role]" plus a time stamp (e.g. 4:00am).
middle: Clips with time labels and voiceover or text commentary.
ending: Wind-down shot, reflection line, or earnings/result.
adapt: Works on every video app. For LinkedIn, frame it around the job ('day in the life of a solo SaaS founder').

name: Wait for it / delayed payoff
structure: Build tension with an on-screen promise of a payoff, then deliver it in the last seconds.
hook: Text overlay: "wait for it…" or "watch till the end" over an ordinary-looking setup.
middle: Slow build with nothing given away.
ending: Twist or reveal in the final 1–3s. Short enough that people replay it.
adapt: Keep the loop tight. Shorts gets the most out of it because it counts replays.

name: Captioned podcast / interview clip
structure: The strongest 30–90s from a long conversation, reframed vertically with big captions.
hook: The most controversial or funny line within 2s, and a title bar.
middle: Uncut exchange with speaker-tracked framing.
ending: Laugh or punchline; cut before the energy drops.
adapt: Most-cross-posted format of all. On LinkedIn, lead with the business quote in text.

name: What $X gets you in [place]
structure: Show exactly what a fixed budget buys in a specific place.
hook: "What $100 gets you at [Walmart / NYC / the Apple Store]".
middle: Items added with a running total.
ending: Final haul and verdict.
adapt: The running total needs burned-in text. Travels as-is.

name: Behind the scenes / how we made it
structure: Reveal the setup behind a finished result.
hook: The finished result, then "here's how we made it".
middle: Rig, set, or process footage.
ending: Side-by-side of BTS vs final.
adapt: For brands, LinkedIn is strong for BTS of launches or campaigns.

name: "Things that just make sense" roundup
structure: A quick tour of clever details in a place or setup.
hook: "Things in [Japan / our salon / my house] that just make sense".
middle: One detail per 2–4s clip, with a label or a pointing gesture.
ending: The best detail last.
adapt: The business version ('things in our office/app that just make sense') is a light brand post on any platform.

name: I asked ChatGPT/AI to…
structure: Give an AI a prompt on screen and react to the result.
hook: The prompt as text ("ChatGPT, show me an apple").
middle: The AI output (screen recording or skit), escalating.
ending: Absurd final output or reaction.
adapt: Screen-recording versions also do well on X and LinkedIn.

name: "Tell me you're X without telling me"
structure: Show one telling detail that identifies a group without naming it.
hook: Text: "Tell me you're [X] without telling me you're [X]".
middle: One visual 'proof' moment.
ending: The reveal is the proof itself.
adapt: Mostly 2021–22 examples. Still recognizable, but not rising.

name: Insider confession ("things I'd never do as a [job]")
structure: A credentialed professional lists what they personally avoid.
hook: "Things I would NEVER buy as a lawyer", with the credential in the first line.
middle: 3–5 items, each with the insider reason.
ending: The most surprising item, then 'follow for more'.
adapt: Ideal LinkedIn text post: 'As a [role] for 10 years, 5 things I'd never do'.

name: Stop doing this / myth vs fact
structure: Call out a common behavior as wrong, then show the fix.
hook: "Stop doing this" with the wrong behavior on screen.
middle: Why it's wrong, then the correct method.
ending: Before/after result or a 'do this instead' recap.
adapt: LinkedIn/X text: 'Stop doing X. Do Y.' works as a one-liner post.

name: Product finds roundup (N things I bought)
structure: Rapid list of products with a demo of each.
hook: "Coolest things I bought on Amazon this month" plus the first product in use.
middle: One product per 3–8s, showing it in use.
ending: Best product last; link-in-bio or storefront CTA.
adapt: Travels as-is. IG/TikTok need an affiliate or storefront link; on Shorts put the link in a pinned comment.

name: I tried X for 30 days
structure: A personal experiment with day markers and a result reveal.
hook: "I tried [creatine / 100 situps] for 30 days" plus Day 1 footage.
middle: Day markers (1, 7, 15, 30) with honest check-ins.
ending: Before/after comparison and verdict.
adapt: Series variant (Day 1/30 daily posts) is TikTok-native. The recap version travels everywhere and doubles as a LinkedIn 'I tried X for 30 days, here's what happened'.

name: Pack an order with me (small business)
structure: ASMR packing of a real customer order, addressed to the customer by name.
hook: "Hi [name], this is your order packing video".
middle: Items added one by one, extras, wrapping.
ending: Sealed box, thank-you note.
adapt: TikTok hits run 4–17 min. Trim to 60s for Shorts/Reels; the addressed-to-customer hook still works.

name: "Things you should never do" numbered list
structure: A numbered list of warnings for a place, time, or situation.
hook: "Never do these things in [China] / at night".
middle: 3–5 items, each with a visual and a one-line why.
ending: The most surprising item last.
adapt: Faceless versions travel best. Post the list as a carousel on IG/LinkedIn.

name: Red flags / green flags
structure: List warning signs (or good signs) in a person, job, or product.
hook: "🚩 red flags in [a partner / a job / a client]".
middle: One flag per beat, often acted out.
ending: The most controversial flag; "many people fall for the last one".
adapt: The client/job red-flags version works as a LinkedIn text post.

name: Tweet/text screenshot carousel
structure: One tweet-style card per slide, 30–60 words each.
hook: The strongest insight as slide 1.
middle: More cards in the same template (color tint changes per slide).
ending: None needed; the caption asks a question.
adapt: Native on X as a text post. On IG/LinkedIn it's a carousel; on TikTok, a photo slideshow with audio.

name: Learn X in 3 steps
structure: Break a hard skill into 3 progressive steps.
hook: "How to [backflip] in only 3 steps" plus the finished move.
middle: Step 1, 2, 3, each with a demo and a text label.
ending: The full move, and 'save this'.
adapt: The same steps can go out as a carousel or a LinkedIn how-to.

name: Mistakes beginners make
structure: Show common beginner mistakes, each followed by the fix.
hook: "Top 3 mistakes [violin / crochet / new writers] beginners make".
middle: Mistake shown, then the correct way.
ending: The biggest mistake last, or 'which one are you guilty of?'.
adapt: Converts directly to a carousel (marketingharry 'UGLY FONTS KILL POSTS' is the carousel version).

name: Faceless top-5 countdown compilation
structure: Countdown of clips ranked 5 to 1 with a ranking bar on the side.
hook: "Top 5 most [dangerous sea creatures]" plus clip #5.
middle: Clips 4 to 2 with the rank overlay updating.
ending: #1 is the most extreme clip.
adapt: Often uses third-party clips, which carry copyright/unoriginal-content risk on YouTube. Using your own footage travels unchanged.

name: Relatable "when you…" meme video
structure: Text caption of a universal moment over a reaction clip or performance.
hook: "When you realize…" caption.
middle: A single reaction beat, often lip-sync or trending audio.
ending: Loop.
adapt: Relies on trending audio that may be unavailable on other apps. Swap to original audio or royalty-free sound when cross-posting.
good_for: any niche with in-jokes (SMM, devs, teachers)

name: Asking 100 people / survey montage
structure: Pose one question to a big number of people and show the tally.
hook: "We asked 100 [group] about X".
middle: Rapid answers with a running count.
ending: The final tally, or the most unexpected answer.
adapt: The B2B version ('we asked 100 marketers') becomes a data carousel or LinkedIn post with the stat.

name: Green screen reaction to a screenshot/post
structure: The creator in front of a screenshot (tweet, headline, comment, Reddit post) reads it and reacts or explains.
hook: The screenshot fills the background; the creator points at it and reads the key line.
middle: Commentary, context, or storytime about it.
ending: Opinion, question to the audience, or the next screenshot.
adapt: TikTok's green-screen effect has no IG/YT equivalent. Record it with TikTok or CapCut and export the file; the output travels unchanged.

name: GRWM storytime (talk while doing a routine)
structure: Tell a story or rant while doing makeup, cooking, or cleaning on camera.
hook: The story's most shocking line first ("we almost lost…").
middle: The routine as visual filler, the story as the content.
ending: Resolution or 'part 2'.
adapt: The TikTok hits run 5–10 min. Cut a 60–90s version with the payoff for Reels/Shorts.

name: Things I regret buying (de-influencing)
structure: Honest list of purchases that weren't worth it.
hook: "Things I regret buying" with the first item held up.
middle: Item, why it failed, and what to buy instead.
ending: The biggest regret or the one they'd buy again.
adapt: SaaS variant: 'tools I stopped paying for'. Works as a LinkedIn text post too.

name: How much I make / income breakdown
structure: Reveal real earnings for a job or shift, itemized.
hook: "How much I make as a [job]" or "how much I made working a double".
middle: Itemized numbers on screen (tips, clients, platform payouts).
ending: The total, with an honest take (worth it or not).
adapt: Travels as-is. LinkedIn/X: an income screenshot plus a breakdown text post (a proven X format).

name: Video reply to a comment
structure: A comment sticker on screen, then the creator answers it on video.
hook: The comment bubble ("Replying to @user…") shown in frame 1.
middle: Direct answer, demo, or clapback.
ending: Invite the next question.
adapt: The native comment sticker exists on TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and IG. When cross-posting, burn in a screenshot of the comment so it reads on every app.
good_for: any niche with an audience asking questions

name: Text/TTS storytime over gameplay or satisfying b-roll
structure: A written story (often from Reddit) read by text-to-speech over unrelated looping footage.
hook: The first line of the story as a title card ("My sister asked why her husband came home at 3am…").
middle: TTS narration with word-by-word captions over Minecraft parkour, cake-cutting, or slime.
ending: Cliffhanger or 'part 2' to drive follows.
adapt: TikTok allows long parts; Shorts caps at 3 min and Reels at 3 min, so split into parts. Commonly flagged as unoriginal on YouTube, so change the story and voice.

name: Numbered list carousel
structure: A cover promising N items, then numbered items across slides with continuous numbering.
hook: Slide 1: "25 lessons…" / "7 practices that…" plus a swipe cue.
middle: 3–4 numbered items per slide or one per slide, same template.
ending: Recap slide plus a save/share or comment-keyword CTA.
adapt: IG and LinkedIn take the same PDF/image set (LinkedIn wants a PDF document post). TikTok photo mode needs a 9:16 or 3:4 crop. X takes up to 4 images, so split it or post as a thread.

name: Notes-app / plain text card
structure: A screenshot of the iPhone Notes app (or a plain black card) carrying a confession, list, or question.
hook: A familiar Notes UI with a first line that reads like a private thought.
middle: List or short rant in plain text.
ending: A question that invites confessional comments.
adapt: The TikTok version is a 6s slideshow with audio. On IG/X/LinkedIn post the static screenshot (influencersinthewild's question card got 52.7K likes and 1,121 comments).

name: Selfie cover + list slides (TikTok photo mode)
structure: Casual selfie with native text as the cover; the following slides are a Notes-app or plain list of tips, apps, or brands.
hook: Selfie plus "I've been posting consistently for 3 months and these are the 4 things I learnt".
middle: 1 item per slide (app, brand plus email, tip), often over a photo.
ending: The last tip plugs a tool or resource, or 'save this'.
adapt: Built for TikTok photo mode with a trending sound. Repost to IG as a carousel (add the music in the IG app). The 'Part N' website series (@lucaswebq, 2.6M plays at part 772) shows how well it serializes.
